content: h07. **Request path:** the browser loads `` — that URL is minted server-side at `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36` (`/file/%s/avatar` from the canonical user name), so viewing another user's profile hits a plain HTTP GET on the fileserver router, not the gRPC/Connect API. Hops: - `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` (route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125 - `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` (serving handler) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168-210 - `FileServerService.getCurrentUser` → `auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` (only when `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is false — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:173-181) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708-712 → server/auth/authenticator.go:190 - `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715-717 - `store.Store.GetUser` (cache check by ID, else delegates) — store/user.go:148-169 - `store.Store.ListUsers` (populates `userCache`) — store/user.go:136-146 - `driver.ListUsers` (interface dispatch) — store/driver.go - `sqlite.DB.ListUsers` — `SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user WHERE username = ?` — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88, query at 151-165, scan into `store.User.AvatarURL` at 182-197 (peer drivers: store/db/mysql/user.go, store/db/postgres/user.go) **Then back out:** `FileServerService.parseDataURI` decodes the stored value — the avatar is *not* a blob in a separate table, it's a base64 `data:` URI held in the `user.avatar_url` column (server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737-745) — the MIME type is checked against `avatarAllowedTypes`, security headers plus `Cache-Control` are set, and the bytes go out via `c.Blob` (fileserver.go:196-209). Two access-control notes worth flagging: authentication is required only on private instances (no `InstanceURL` ⇒ `AllowAnonymous()` false, internal/profile/profile.go:46) and there is no per-user authorization check — any authenticated viewer, or anyone at all on a public instance, can fetch any username's avatar. The route also resolves usernames only, not numeric IDs (comment at fileserver.go:714).
